title: Ideal-power conductor multiplication
statement: For a finite intermediate B-subalgebra A of the fraction field K, assume r satisfies the conductor property: for every b in J(B)^r and every a in A, the product b*a comes from B. Then for z in (J(B)A)^r and every a in A, the product z*a comes from B.

proof.text: Rewrite (map J(B))^r as map (J(B)^r) using Mathlib Ideal.map_pow. Its membership is membership in the ideal span of mapped base elements. Apply Submodule.span_induction, keeping the multiplier arbitrary. On generators apply the assumed conductor property; use the base-ring witnesses 0 and c+d for zero and addition. For t*z absorb t into the arbitrary multiplier and commute the factors.

proof_origin.note: U3: corrected the missing suitable-exponent hypothesis and proved extension to the ideal map by Mathlib span induction.

lean.statement:
theorem Subalgebra.exists_base_mul_mem_of_mem_map_jacobson_pow
    {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [IsDomain B] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    [Finite (MaximalSpectrum B)] (hdim : ringKrullDim B = 1)
    {K : Type v} [Field K] [Algebra B K] [IsFractionRing B K]
    (A : Subalgebra B K) [Module.Finite B A] [IsFractionRing A K]
    {r : ℕ}
    (hconductor : ∀ b : B, b ∈ (Ideal.jacobson (⊥ : Ideal B)) ^ r →
      ∀ a : A, ∃ c : B, algebraMap B K c = algebraMap B K b * (a : K))
    (z : A)
    (hz : z ∈ (Ideal.map (algebraMap B A) (Ideal.jacobson (⊥ : Ideal B))) ^ r)
    (a : A) : ∃ c : B, algebraMap B K c = (z : K) * (a : K)

statement_change.old_statement: For a finite intermediate B-subalgebra A of the fraction field K and z in (J(B)A)^r, every product z*a with a in A comes from B.
statement_change.what: STATEMENT-DISPUTED: the arbitrary exponent r is not a conductor exponent. At r=0 and z=1 the original would force A=image(B); the cusp local ring B=Q[t^2,t^3]_(t^2,t^3), A=B[t], K=Q(t), a=t is a counterexample. Add the base-ring conductor property for r, exactly the property of the suitable exponent in Stacks 09N2, already available at the caller.

citers.note: The caller already obtains r with its conductor property from lem-sc-finite-integral-conductor. Retain that property and pass it to the corrected lemma; its conclusion and the caller statement are unchanged.

old_proof.text: Expand membership in the ideal power as finite sums of products of mapped Jacobson elements, apply the finite conductor theorem termwise, and sum the resulting base elements.
